candidates.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
Diffusion transformers with hybrid conditioning for structural optimization
candidates.abstract: Abstract This work presents a diffusion transformer framework for data-driven structural topology optimization that combines the accuracy of physics-based methods with the efficiency of generative deep learning. Conventional density-based approaches which use the solid isotropic material with penalization (SIMP) scheme with a gradient update require repeated finite element analyses at every iteration, making large-scale or real-time optimization computationally expensive. We propose a hybrid conditioning diffusion transformer (DiT) model that learns to generate near-optimal topologies directly from problem definitions, eliminating iterative analysis during inference. The model integrates spatially distributed conditioning through concatenated stress and strain fields and global conditioning via adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) using scalar descriptors such as load position, magnitude, and prescribed volume fraction. A dataset of 30,000 two-dimensional SIMP-optimized structures was generated for training and evaluation. Results demonstrate that the proposed DiT achieves less than 1% compliance errors relative to ground-truth SIMP solutions while maintaining accurate volume fractions and structural connectivity. Deterministic DDIM sampling enables high-fidelity topology generation in seconds using as few as five denoising steps, enabling near-real-time performance. The hybrid conditioning diffusion transformer thus provides an efficient and scalable alternative to traditional topology optimization methods, with strong potential for integration into interactive computer-aided design workflows.

candidates.title: Performance of large language models in complex coronary artery disease decision-making and potential improvement strategy in a real-world cohort
candidates.abstract: Objective Previous studies have demonstrated that large language models (LLMs) can achieve performance comparable to multidisciplinary heart teams (HTs) in coronary revascularisation decision-making but limited by population bias. We aimed to assess LLMs’ performance in complex coronary artery disease (CAD) decision-making using a real-world cohort and to explore the potential improvement strategy.Methods Patients with stable CAD and angiographically confirmed three-vessel or left main disease randomly selected from a consecutive angiography registry study were included in this cross-sectional study. ChatGPT-4.1 was used to provide five-category treatment decisions based on inputted patient information and a prompt most commonly used by real-world patients. The primary outcome was the agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations. Three predefined prompting strategies were further evaluated for their potential to enhance agreement rates.Results A total of 564 patients were included. The agreement rate between HT and LLM recommendations was 47.0% based on initial prompt. LLM performed poorly in further testing (sensitivity=0.0%) decision. LLM performed well in patients with Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with Taxus and Cardiac Surgery score ≥33 (94.1%) but poorly in 23–32 (61.7%) and 0–22 (20.9%). After using prompting strategies, the agreement rate increased significantly (79.3%, p<0.001).Discussion Simple patient-style queries cannot independently generate reliable decisions for real-world complex revascularisation scenarios. While prompt engineering and subgroup analysis can partially improve LLM’s performance, the potential safety risk remains emphasised.Conclusion Among a real-world cohort of patients with complex CAD, the agreement rate of decision-making between LLM and HTs was only half, but could be improved with appropriate prompts.

candidates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Driven Augmentation With Deep Feature Fusion Model for Rare Disease Detection and Classification
candidates.abstract: Rare disease detection focuses on identifying rare health conditions that affect a tiny fraction of people. Detection is challenging because symptoms are often ambiguous and information is limited. In recent years, retinal diseases have become a serious problem worldwide. Progressing a computer-assisted diagnosis (CAD) method is highly beneficial and functional for ophthalmologists. Proper detection and treatment can save eye vision. Deep learning (DL) has advanced across various scientific fields and is leveraged for numerous healthcare tasks. This research presents a Generative Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Adaptive Feature Fusion Network for Rare Retinal Disease Detection (GAIAFF-RRDD) technique assists ophthalmologists by allowing early and precise detection of rare retinal diseases, thus enhancing clinical decision-making and decreasing diagnostic workload. The GAIAFF-RRDD technique integrates advanced pre-processing, augmentation, feature fusion, and classification strategies to improve diagnostic accuracy in retinal image analysis. A conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) is employed to augment realistic images and overcome the limited availability of images for rare retinal diseases. Furthermore, adaptive feature fusion is performed by combining features extracted from CapsNet, DenseNet-121, and VGG-16 methods. Finally, a variational autoencoder (VAE)-based classification technique is used to classify rare retinal diseases accurately. To ensure improved performance of the GAIAFF-RRDD methodology, an extensive simulation analysis is conducted using the RFMiD dataset. The comparison study of the GAIAFF-RRDD methodology showed an accuracy of 93.92% compared with existing approaches. Therefore, the proposed model is found to be a robust tool for automated and accurate rare disease detection process.
candidates.venue: Iraqi Journal of Computer Communication Control and System Engineering

candidates.title: Comparison of Integrated Versus Sequential Artificial Intelligence–Based Computer-Aided Diagnosis Systems in Breast Ultrasound: A Prospective Pilot Study on Examination Time, Reproducibility, and Diagnostic Performance
candidates.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To compare integrated and sequential artificial intelligence-based computer-aided diagnosis (AI-CAD) systems in terms of examination time, reproducibility, and diagnostic performance in breast ultrasound (US). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective single-center study included women who underwent breast US at a breast imaging center between February and March 2025. Two real-time AI-CAD systems were evaluated: an integrated system providing simultaneous lesion detection and diagnosis during scanning, and a sequential system in which lesion detection and diagnostic assessment were performed separately. Examination time was assessed in patients who underwent paired breast US examinations with both AI-CAD systems during the same visit, with randomized examination order. Reproducibility was assessed by applying both systems twice to the same breast lesions. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). RESULTS: Examination time analysis included 97 patients and showed longer examination time with sequential AI-CAD than with integrated AI-CAD (P < .001), regardless of examination order. Reproducibility analysis included 145 patients with 215 lesions and showed almost perfect agreement between the first and second acquisitions for both systems (integrated vs. sequential: κ = 0.81 vs. 0.83). For the comparison between the first and second acquisitions, κ values for the integrated versus sequential systems were 0.92 versus 0.76 for malignant lesions, 0.79 versus 0.84 for mass lesions, and 1.00 versus 0.75 for nonmass lesions. However, agreement patterns varied across other scan-plane comparisons. Diagnostic performance analysis included 242 patients. Integrated AI-CAD showed higher sensitivity (integrated vs. sequential: 87.6% vs. 76.9%; P < .001), whereas sequential AI-CAD showed higher specificity (integrated vs. sequential: 74.2% vs. 90.0%; P < .001). AUC did not differ between the two systems. CONCLUSION: Integrated and sequential AI-CAD systems showed complementary strengths in breast US. Integrated AI-CAD favored shorter examination time and higher sensitivity, whereas sequential AI-CAD favored higher specificity, with reproducibility differing according to lesion type.

candidates.title: Revolutionizing Failure Analysis: Physics-Guided AI for Advanced Technology CAD Alignment
candidates.abstract: Abstract This paper presents an automated system for accurately aligning infrared (IR) and computer-aided design (CAD) images. Accurate alignment is an important prerequisite for successful defect localization in failure analysis (FA). Building on the authors' prior study at a different semiconductor technology node, the approach leverages in-depth knowledge of the semiconductor fabrication process, deep neural networks, and computer vision algorithms to achieve precise alignment. The results demonstrate high alignment accuracy using synthetic IR images.
candidates.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

candidates.title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Reliability Assessment Methodology for Total Ionizing Dose Effects in FDSOI MOSFETs
candidates.abstract: This work investigates the effects of total ionizing dose (TID) on 22 nm FDSOI MOSFET devices through combined technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations and actual TID irradiation experiments, establishing a comprehensive dataset of radiation-induced degradation characteristics. By utilizing both simulated and experimental radiation data as training foundations, this research developed and optimized a deep neural network (DNN) capable of conducting efficient and accurate reliability analysis of TID effects under various radiation conditions, with demonstrated effectiveness in predicting device performance degradation across different TID ranges. The methodology integrates physical simulations with deep learning approaches, where TCAD simulations and irradiation experiments capture fundamental device physics under radiation exposure, while the DNN enables rapid performance prediction. The resulting framework achieves superior prediction accuracy while significantly reducing computational costs compared to conventional simulation methods, providing a powerful solution for evaluating electronic device reliability in complex radiation environments.

candidates.title: OP-CAD: On-Policy Clean-Audio Distillation for Robust Audio-Visual Reasoning
candidates.abstract: Omni-modal large language models deployed in real-world environments encounter external noise that can interfere with their perception and understanding of multimodal inputs. We study their robustness in audio-visual understanding, focusing on question answering under environmental noise and competing speech. The challenge is to resist acoustic interference while preserving useful audio evidence. On-policy distillation provides dense teacher feedback on student-generated responses, but uniform token weighting does not explicitly prioritize positions affected by acoustic interference. We introduce OP-CAD (On-Policy Clean-Audio Distillation), a curriculum-based privileged self-distillation framework for robust audio-visual understanding. Training progresses from mild to severe environmental noise and competing speech, with selective token-level supervision at each stage. The student generates responses from corrupted audio-visual input, while a frozen teacher uses clean audio and the verified answer to supervise the same response prefixes. To allocate this supervision, OP-CAD compares teacher predictions under clean, corrupted, and visual-only contexts without revealing the answer. These matched comparisons measure sensitivity to audio removal and corruption; a bounded weighting rule emphasizes positions identified by either signal while retaining supervision throughout the response. OP-CAD outperforms the compared methods across all evaluated noise conditions. Paired analyses further show improved preservation of clean-correct answers under strong interference, with no observed aggregate clean-accuracy penalty. These results demonstrate the value of directing clean-teacher supervision toward acoustically sensitive predictions for robust audio-visual reasoning.

candidates.title: Comparison of AI-generated and conventional CAD/CAM crown designs: An in vitro evaluation
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can automate crown design, but its accuracy and function require comparison with conventional CAD/CAM. Therefore, it is of interest to compare the both workflows on 30 standardized mandibular first-molar preparations. AI shortened design time (1.73 ą 0.43 vs 5.63 ą 1.14 min; p<0.001) and reduced whole-crown RMS deviation. AI reduced marginal gap (60.3 ą 14.2 versus 68.8 ą 13.0 ľm; p<0.001), while conventional CAD was better proximally. Thus, functional contacts were comparable, supporting AI as an efficient design aid with final technician or clinician verification.

candidates.title: Agent Breast-RAG: An Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Explainable Large Language Model Framework for Multimodal Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Clinical Decision Support
candidates.abstract: Breast cancer continues to be one of the leading causes of cancer-related death among women worldwide, and early detection together with timely clinical intervention remains essential for improving survival outcomes. Deep learning and Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive results in breast cancer diagnosis and medical decision support, yet their use in real clinical settings is still held back by black-box decision making, hallucinated outputs, reasoning that is not grounded in evidence, poor integration of heterogeneous patient data, and limited explainability. Most existing computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems focus mainly on image classification and offer little in the way of transparent clinical justification or personalized treatment guidance, which in turn undermines clinician trust and everyday usefulness. This paper proposes AgentBreast-RAG, an Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Explainable Large Language Model (ARX-LLM) framework built for breast cancer diagnosis and clinical decision support. The framework brings together multimodal patient data, mammography, ultrasound and histopathological imaging, clinical records, laboratory findings, biomarker profiles, and patient history, within a single diagnostic pipeline that is coordinated by a collaborative multi-agent ecosystem. Within this ecosystem, specialized agents handle patient profiling, medical image interpretation, evidence retrieval, clinical reasoning, explanation generation, treatment recommendation, and decision verification. An Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG) module retrieves and verifies medical evidence from PubMed, NCCN guidelines, ASCO recommendations, WHO resources, and peer-reviewed oncology literature in a dynamic, ongoing manner, which substantially cuts down hallucination compared to standalone LLMs. A dedicated Explainable AI (XAI) module then brings all of this together through Grad-CAM and attention visualization for imaging, SHAP-based feature attribution for structured variables, natural-language rationales grounded in the retrieved evidence, and an uncertainty estimation module that assigns confidence scores to the model's outputs. We also lay out an evaluation protocol built around seven public multimodal breast cancer resources (CBIS-DDSM, INbreast, BUSI, BreakHis, BACH, the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Dataset, and TCGA-BRCA), benchmarked against convolutional neural networks, Vision Transformers, conventional RAG, GraphRAG, and existing medical LLMs. This evaluation draws on diagnostic metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Specificity, Sensitivity, AUC), retrieval metrics (Recall@K, Precision@K, nDCG), and explainability metrics (faithfulness, localization accuracy, clinician interpretability rating, hallucination rate). The performance figures reported here are illustrative and clearly labeled as simulated projections rather than results from executed experiments; they are meant only to show the intended structure of the evaluation. Even so, the direction we propose suggests that combining autonomous multi-agent collaboration, verified retrieval, multimodal fusion, and interpretable decision support could meaningfully improve diagnostic reliability, evidence-grounded reasoning, and clinician confidence, pointing toward a scalable path for trustworthy, explainable AI-assisted breast cancer care.

candidates.title: A Study on Innovation Strategies in Contemporary Jewelry Design Using Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: 본 연구의 목적은 생성형 인공지능(AI) 기술을 활용한 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략을 고찰하고, AI 기술이 디자인 창작과 제작 과정에 미치는 영향과 활용 가능성을 분석하는 데 있다. 최근 생성형 AI의 발전은 디자인 분야 전반에 새로운 창작 환경을 제시하고 있으며, 현대 주얼리 디자인에서도 아이디어 발상, 형태 생성, 맞춤형 제작, 디지털 제작 공정 등 다양한 영역으로 활용 범위가 확대되고 있다. 이에 본 연구는 생성형 AI 기술이 현대 주얼리 디자인에 가져온 변화와 혁신 전략을 체계적으로 분석하고 그 의의를 도출하고자 하였다. 연구방법은 문헌연구와 내용분석을 중심으로 진행하였다. 국내외 학술논문, 전문서적, 학회자료 및 산업보고서를 검토하여 생성형 AI의 개념과 특성을 정리하고, 현대 주얼리 디자인과의 연계 가능성을 고찰하였다. 또한 생성형 AI 도구와 보조 디자인 시스템의 기능 및 활용 특성을 분석하여 기술 활용의 특징을 도출하고, 이를 바탕으로 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략을 종합적으로 분석하였다. 연구 결과, 생성형 AI는 현대 주얼리 디자인의 기획, 설계 및 제작 전 과정에서 활용되며 디자인 프로세스를 확장하는 핵심 기술로 확인되었다. 내용분석에서는 생성형 AI가 다양한 디자인 아이디어를 신속하게 제안하고, 복합적인 형태 생성과 사용자 맞춤형 디자인을 구현하며, CAD와 3D 프린팅 등 디지털 제작 기술과 연계되어 제작 효율성과 표현 가능성을 향상시키는 것으로 나타났다. 이를 바탕으로 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략은 첫째, 사용자의 취향과 요구를 반영하는 개별 맞춤형 제작과 둘째, 생성형 AI, CAD, 파라메트릭 모델링 및 3D 프린팅 기술을 활용한 기술 중심의 형태 및 공정 혁신으로 구분할 수 있었다. 개별 맞춤형 제작은 소비자 중심의 디자인 환경을 확대하고 감성적 가치를 높이는 데 기여하였으며, 형태 및 공정 혁신은 복합적인 형태 구현, 설계 오류 감소, 제작 기간 단축 및 생산 효율 향상에 기여하는 것으로 분석되었다. 결론적으로 생성형 AI는 현대 주얼리 디자인에서 창의성 확장, 맞춤형 디자인 구현 및 제작 공정의 효율화를 실현하는 핵심 기술로서 디자인 혁신을 촉진하는 중요한 역할을 수행하고 있다. 특히 AI는 디자이너를 대체하는 기술이 아니라 창의적 사고를 지원하고 디지털 제작 환경과 연계하는 협업 도구로서의 가능성을 보여준다. 본 연구는 생성형 AI 기반 현대 주얼리 디자인의 혁신 전략을 체계적으로 정리하였다는 점에서 학술적 의의를 가지며, 향후 AI 기술과 주얼리 디자인의 융합에 관한 후속 연구를 위한 기초자료로 활용될 수 있을 것으로 기대한다.

candidates.title: CANTO: CAD-Native Transformer Operators for AI-Aided Engineering
candidates.abstract: Modern engineering systems, from automobiles to aircraft, are designed by using precise, continuous parametric computer-aided design (CAD) models. Evaluating design changes through numerical simulation requires meshing the continuous geometry, a computationally expensive and often brittle process that can require manual intervention and replaces the continuous representation with a discrete approximation. Most neural surrogates accelerate the simulation, but inherit this representation gap by relying on meshes, point clouds, voxels, or other sampled approximations of geometry. We introduce CANTO, a transformer neural operator that maps directly from continuous CAD geometry to physical fields, without meshing the input geometry. We develop a theoretical framework for learning operators from geometric manifolds to function spaces of physical fields, representing geometry through sequences of parametric patches. CANTO instantiates this framework by directly tokenizing non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) patches from their control points, knot vectors, and weights, and predicts continuous surface and volume fields at arbitrary query locations. We evaluate CANTO on four automotive and aircraft aerodynamics industry benchmarks: AhmedML, WindsorML, DrivAerML, and HiLiftAeroML. CANTO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on most evaluated surface and volume prediction tasks, including a 19.8% reduction in surface-pressure relative $L_2$ error compared with AB-UPT on HiLiftAeroML. Differentiability with respect to CAD parameters further enables gradient-based inverse design of designs. On AhmedML, CANTO identifies designs with 4.4 to 20.4% lower drag than the best dataset designs satisfying the same volume and lift constraints, with the improvements verified using the same CFD setup used to generate the original dataset.

candidates.title: From Concept to Reality: AI Model Implementation Driving Operational Excellence in Oil & Gas Engineering Design
candidates.abstract: Abstract Engineering design for oil and gas facilities remains labor‑intensive, particularly in the production of Computer Aided Design (CAD) deliverables such as Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), isometrics, and 3D pipe routing. Advances in AI and learning‑based generative/optimization methods, now enable partial to substantial automation of drawing creation, model verification, and data enrichment. This paper presents a practical, end‑to‑end AI implementation that accelerates concept‑to‑detail design workflows while maintaining conformance with engineering standards and plant data models. Furthermore, this paper summarizes state of the art evidence, detailing a modular architecture that digitizes legacy drawings, auto routes pipework, programmatically generates isometrics, and quantify reductions in manual drafting hours.
candidates.venue: SPE Gulf Oil and Gas Technology Conference (GOTECH)

candidates.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
candidates.abstract: Autonomous agents have made rapid progress in general-purpose computer use, yet reliable automation of professional industrial engineering remains out of reach. Engineering workflows require reasoning over geometric and physical constraints and keeping dependencies consistent across software and design stages. We present EngiWorld, a benchmark designed around the capabilities that real engineering projects require, from operating a single application to solving engineering problems end to end. It contains 1,301 expert-curated tasks spanning six engineering domains (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, and DCC) and 26 professional software applications, with both GUI and CLI interfaces. The tasks are organized into six types, corresponding to capabilities that real engineering projects require. We further introduce an artifact-centric evaluation methodology built on a unified suite of domain verifiers. The verifiers programmatically check whether final and intermediate artifacts are geometrically valid, physically feasible, and compliant with design rules. Beyond binary success, they also score how well optimized designs meet their specifications. Evaluation of seven frontier models reveals a substantial capability gap: the strongest model scores only 44.7/100, and just 3.6% of runs on tasks that require cross-software coordination succeed. EngiWorld provides a rigorous foundation for measuring progress toward agents that operate professional engineering software end to end.

candidates.title: Comparing Deep Learning Models for Lung Nodule Detection on Photon-Counting CT Images in a Non-Screening Setting
candidates.abstract: Abstract Background Comprehensive evaluations of lung nodule detection methods remain limited, particularly regarding data from clinical routine, novel photon-counting CT (PCCT) technology, and the comparison of academic and commercial models. Materials and Methods This retrospective study collected 1860 routine PCCT scans acquired at Hannover Medical School from 2021 to 2024. We compared four deep-learning-based lung nodule detection models, which were developed for conventional CT, namely the publicly available TotalSegmentator, nnDetection, and RadYOLO methods, as well as a commercial lung computer-aided detection (CAD) system. We evaluated the inter-model agreement in an unannotated cohort (n=1699), sensitivity in a smaller cohort of 25 manually annotated scans, and false positives as detections in 136 report-negative scans. Results In the unannotated cohort, the commercial CAD system detected 7071, TotalSegmentator 4264, nnDetection 5254, and RadYOLO 3122 nodules. Overall, the inter-model agreement was low, and the models produced substantially different candidate nodules. Approximately 1300 nodules were detected by all models, representing 18.7% - 42.8% of each model’s detections. 15.4% - 37.4% of a model’s detections did not match any other model. The models showed moderate sensitivity (between 0.71, 95%-CI [0.64, 0.77], and 0.83, 95%-CI [0.77, 0.88]), and TotalSegmentator and RadYOLO produced few false positives per scan (both 0.85, 95%-CI [0.70, 1.02]). Conclusion The lung nodules detected by four deep learning models showed high variation and a lack of consensus on clinical PCCT data. These findings highlight the importance of model benchmarking and local validation when deploying models in real-world clinical workflows.

candidates.title: An Integrative Review of Innovations and Ethical Dimensions in Modern Plastic Surgery
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Plastic surgery has evolved from a specialty primarily focused on reconstructive and cosmetic procedures into a multidisciplinary field encompassing regenerative surgery, aesthetic medicine, and advanced technological innovations. Recent developments in microsurgery, artificial intelligence (AI), three-dimensional (3D) modelling, image-guided surgical planning, tissue engineering, and stem cell-based therapies have significantly improved surgical precision, patient safety, and personalized treatment outcomes. This review summarizes current innovations while addressing the ethical and regulatory challenges associated with their clinical implementation. Methods: A comprehensive narrative literature review was conducted using electronic databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, covering publications from 2010 to 2025. Relevant peer-reviewed articles were identified using keywords related to reconstructive surgery, aesthetic surgery, regenerative medicine, stem cells, tissue engineering, microsurgery, biomaterials, artificial intelligence, and 3D modelling. The selected literature was critically evaluated to summarize recent technological advances, clinical applications, regenerative strategies, and ethical considerations in modern plastic surgery. Results: The review demonstrates that advances in microsurgical reconstruction, CAD/CAM technologies, image-guided surgery, AI-assisted planning, minimally invasive aesthetic procedures, regenerative medicine, stem cell therapy, growth factors, biomaterials, and tissue engineering have transformed plastic surgery into a highly personalized and precision-based specialty. Discussion: These innovations have enhanced functional restoration, aesthetic outcomes, surgical accuracy, and patient quality of life while reducing complications and recovery time. However, widespread clinical implementation remains limited by challenges including procedural standardization, long-term safety, cost, regulatory approval, ethical concerns, and unequal accessibility. Integrating emerging technologies with evidence-based clinical practice and multidisciplinary collaboration will be essential for achieving sustainable and patient-centred care. Conclusion: Modern plastic surgery is undergoing a paradigm shift toward precision, regenerative, and patient-centred healthcare. Emerging technologies, regenerative therapies, and AI-driven innovations are reshaping reconstructive and aesthetic practice by improving both functional and cosmetic outcomes. Future progress will depend on rigorous clinical validation, standardized treatment protocols, ethical governance, and interdisciplinary research to ensure the safe, effective, and responsible integration of these innovations into routine clinical practice.

candidates.title: Coupling winding-pattern generation with discrete layup optimisation: A computer-aided design framework for manufacturable filament-wound type IV COPVs
candidates.abstract: Filament wound Type IV composite overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) require lightweight layups that remain compatible with feasible winding patterns. Manufacturing feasibility has previously been incorporated into filament wound optimisation through trajectory constraints, feasible angle restrictions and manufacturing informed structural models. In the proposed framework, this manufacturing information is introduced directly at the layer level, with each optimised helical layer represented by a finite set of manufacturable winding pattern candidates. Each candidate is associated with its corrected winding angle, circuit count, turn count, skip index, correction factor, coverage and pattern type. A genetic algorithm explores the resulting combinatorial design space using dual surrogate screening. XGBoost predicts composite mass, while a fine tuned Transformer predicts the layer wise stress response. The retained configuration is subsequently re-evaluated using the WoundSim analytical model and assessed through the WoundSim-Abaqus finite element workflow. For a vessel with 41 optimised helical layers and three candidates per layer, the composite mass decreases from 84.67 kg to 82.38 kg and the maximum analytical fibre direction stress decreases from 2165.14 MPa to 2116.91 MPa, while the cylindrical thickness remains 41.0 mm.

candidates.title: THEIA: A Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Vision-Language Analysis of Layout
candidates.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into computer-aided design frameworks has sparked a shift in the design of analog integrated circuits (ICs), transitioning the field from using manual and algorithmic-based solutions to adopting automated and intelligent paradigms. In this scenario, the GDSII file represents the industry-standard database containing the ultimate and most accurate source of information of the analog circuit, encapsulating the complex physical geometries and parasitic realities that define tape out performance. This paper proposes THEIA, a novel dataset containing thousands of layout images paired with question-answer conversations, along with a benchmark that employs a fine-tuned vision-language model (VLM) to analyze GDSII files of analog circuits, enabling designers to interact with and query physical layouts as intuitive, meaningful entities. Experimental results using thousands of analog designs across five realistic tasks demonstrate that the proposed fine-tuned VLM outperforms state-of-the-art general-purpose VLMs by a significant margin (up to 73%), highlighting a fundamental gap between general-purpose multimodal reasoning and domain-specific layout understanding.

candidates.title: Physics-Inspired Convolutional Neural Network for Tire Tread Pattern Noise Prediction from Digitized Tread Images
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Tire tread pattern noise (TPN) is a dominant acoustic concern in electric vehicle powertrains, where the absence of engine masking makes noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) performance critically dependent on tread geometry. This paper presents a physics-inspired convolutional neural network (CNN) framework, implemented in MATLAB, that predicts TPN directly from digitized tread profile images. Tread images were acquired at 1600 × 412 pixels in grayscale by using a Tire360 three-dimensional scanning system, and acoustic training targets were obtained by applying order-domain synchronous averaging to semi-anechoic chamber measurements, isolating the periodic TPN component from non-tread noise. The training dataset was assembled through a structured design-of-experiments covering pitch sequences, groove, and sipe geometry; multiple tire sizes; and hand-carved tread variants. A novel CNN architecture was developed to accept the binarized images, extract spatial spectral features, and map them onto an 8-point one-third-octave noise spectrum. The trained network was subsequently tested using a design-stage tread pattern generated from computer-aided design, and the predicted spectrum showed good agreement with the corresponding experimental measurement. The results demonstrate that physics-inspired deep learning has promising capability for estimating TPN trends at an early design stage, potentially reducing dependence on physical prototyping and enabling rapid NVH-informed tire development.

candidates.title: Natural-language control of parametric road design based on large language models
candidates.abstract: Background. Natural-language control forms a new direction in the development of road computer-aided design systems. However, direct conversion of an engineering task into a program script by a large language model does not guarantee geometric, computational, or regulatory correctness of the result. Aim: To assess the applicability of large language models to the formation of parametric road-object models and to substantiate an architecture for their safe integration into the design process. Materials and methods: In the FreeCAD environment, the creation of a model of a road sign and a multicomponent fragment of a category II road based on text prompts was studied. Script execution, geometry editability, the number of refinement cycles, and the volume of tokens used were evaluated. Results: The fundamental feasibility of natural-language control over a multi-component road model was demonstrated. It was established that a direct generative approach retains significant engineering labor and requires an external validation loop for geometric, computational, and regulatory compliance. A target control architecture and a reconstruction completeness criterion are proposed. Conclusion: The functional separation among the language model, geometric kernel, validation tools, and engineer forms the foundation for a new generation of intelligent road CAD systems.

candidates.title: Inspector: Conversational and Lightweight Analyzer of Analog Circuit Layouts Using LLM and CNNs
candidates.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into computer-aided design frameworks has sparked a shift in the design of analog integrated circuits (ICs), transitioning the field from using manual and algorithmic-based solutions to adopting automated and intelligent paradigms. In this scenario, the GDSII file represents the industry-standard database containing the ultimate and most accurate source of information of the analog circuit, encapsulating the complex physical geometries and parasitic realities that define tape out performance. This paper proposes a novel framework that combines fine-tuned LLMs and CNNs to analyze GDSII files of analog circuits, enabling a conversational interface between the tool and the designers. Experimental results using thousands of analog designs across four realistic tasks demonstrate that the proposed solution outperforms state-of-the-art general-purpose massive VLMs by a significant margin (up to 81%), thus providing a lightweight solution to the problem of GDSII analysis.

candidates.title: DrawingsDreamer: A Unified Multi-View Engineering Drawings Generation Model
candidates.abstract: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) are essential for modern industrial Computer-Aided Design (CAD). However, existing autoregressive SVG generation models are predominantly tailored for artistic creation and struggle to maintain the rigorous geometric fidelity and cross-view spatial alignment required for engineering drawings. To bridge this gap, we introduce \textbf{DrawingsDreamer}, a unified Large Language Model (LLM)-driven framework for multi-view vector-based engineering drawings generation. By formulating the generation of multi-view engineering drawings purely as a sequence modeling task, we eliminate the need of raster image encoders. We propose a Streamlined Representation utilizing hierarchical postfix tokenization, which guides the model to establish local geometric coordinates before assigning semantic boundaries. Optimized via a progressive task-aware curriculum schedule, \textbf{DrawingsDreamer} effectively transitions from localized structural repair to macroscopic generation in a unified model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our unified model achieves strong performance in both geometric fidelity and syntactic accuracy across diverse conditional and unconditional generation tasks.

candidates.title: Procedural Modelling and Generative AI for Augmented Contextual 3D Visualisation of Planned Urban Change
candidates.abstract: Street-level visualisations play an important role in urban street redesign by helping stakeholders and non-specialist audiences understand proposed spatial transformations. However, conventional image-editing workflows are often time-consuming, while purely image-based generative AI approaches provide limited control over object position, scale, and spatial relationships. This study presents a novel, highly automated workflow combining georeferenced street-level smartphone imagery, procedural 3D modelling, semantic image segmentation, and controlled generative AI to produce realistic visualisations of planned street transformations. Two-dimensional CAD drawings of planned changes are procedurally converted into simplified 3D models. Semantic masks are rendered from georeferenced camera viewpoints in the 3D model and combined with masks extracted from the street-level smartphone images. The resulting semantic and inpainting masks condition a Stable Diffusion XL-based inpainting model through segmentation and Canny-edge ControlNets. Text prompts control the overall visual appearance, while an IP-Adapter enables selected elements, such as vegetation and tree species, to be refined using reference images. The workflow was applied to two street redesign scenarios. The results show that planned elements can be generated at positions and with dimensions closely corresponding to the planning data, while different visual and seasonal variants can be explored without changing the spatial configuration. The method therefore provides a scalable approach for generating street-level visualisations while preserving geometric control.

candidates.title: Classification of HEp-2 Cell Patterns in Autoimmune Disease Diagnosis Using Hybrid DenseNet-ViT Architecture
candidates.abstract: Background/Aim: Accurate and consistent interpretation of HEp-2 cell patterns, considered the gold standard in autoimmune disease diagnosis, remains challenging due to inter-expert variability. This study aims to develop a hybrid deep learning architecture for the automated and highly accurate classification of HEp-2 cell images.Methods: The proposed approach integrates DenseNet-121, which excels at capturing local morphological features, with Vision Transformer (ViT-B16), known for modeling global contextual relationships. These models are combined using a weighted ensemble strategy. The performance of the model was evaluated on the MIVIA (ICPR 2012) dataset under a strict source-image split protocol, which explicitly prevents the object-level data leakage frequently overlooked in the literature.Results: The proposed hybrid model achieved an overall accuracy of 96.01% under these rigorous test conditions, without the use of synthetic data augmentation. A key methodological contribution is its ability to effectively distinguish between Homogeneous and Fine Speckled patterns, which are frequently misclassified by experts. Notably, the model achieved 100% precision for the Fine Speckled class. Additionally, it was empirically demonstrated that a small batch size (Batch Size = 8) improves generalization performance in fine-textured biomedical images.Conclusion: These findings demonstrate the robust feature extraction capabilities of the proposed hybrid architecture, establishing a reliable, realistic, and methodologically transparent baseline for future computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems.
